title: 《高等微積分》第 2 集｜集合、受限變數與關係｜Loomis & Sternberg 第 0 章 §4-6
description:
本集對應 Loomis 與 Sternberg《Advanced Calculus》第 0 章第 4 到 6 節（書頁 6 到 10）。

現在的數學把每一個對象都定義成某種集合，所以要先把這個最基本的概念看清楚。集合是一堆對象的聚集，而這個聚集本身也被當成一個實體。

等號在數學裡表示邏輯上的同一：兩個集合被視為同一個對象，若且唯若它們的成員完全相同。所以集合相等整個化約成一句話——對每一個 x，x 屬於 A 若且唯若 x 屬於 B。如果 A 的每個元素都是 B 的元素，就說 A 包含於 B；於是 A 等於 B 等價於兩個方向的包含同時成立，這正是證明集合相等最常用的辦法。

有限集可以直接把成員列出來，只有一個成員的叫單元集，兩個的叫對集。無限集通常用敘述框架定義，例如平方小於九的所有實數就是開區間負三到三。我們需要空集，就像算術裡需要零一樣；作者順帶提到，四這個數本身通常定義成零一二三所成的集合。

接下來是受限變數。數學裡的變數不能拿任意對象當值，它只能取某個集合裡的成員，這個集合叫做定義域。定義域有時明講，更多時候是隱含的，例如字母 n 通常就代表整數。要注意受限變數只是無限制變數的縮寫，而且兩種展開式不一樣：全稱的情形用蘊涵，存在的情形用「而且」，這兩者不能弄混。

最後是有序對與關係。有序對的關鍵性質是：兩個有序對相等，若且唯若第一個元素相等而且第二個元素相等，所以一三不等於三一。既然關係的圖形是一組有序對，而每個數學對象都被看成集合，那就乾脆讓關係就是它的圖形——一個關係就是一組有序對。由此定義定義域、值域與反關係；第一元素在 A、第二元素在 B 的所有有序對，構成 A 與 B 的笛卡兒積。

本影片為雙語教學動畫系列（繁體中文版）。

title: Advanced Calculus, Episode 2 | Sets, Restricted Variables and Relations | Ch. 0, §4-6
description:
This episode covers chapter 0, sections 4 to 6 (pages 6 to 10) of Loomis and Sternberg's Advanced Calculus.

Modern practice defines every mathematical object as a set of some kind, so this notion has to be examined first. A set is a collection of objects that is itself considered an entity.

The equals sign means logical identity: two sets are the same object if and only if they have exactly the same members. So set equality reduces to a single line, that for every x, x belongs to A if and only if x belongs to B. If every element of A is an element of B then A is included in B, and A equals B is equivalent to both inclusions holding, which is the usual way set identity actually gets proved.

A finite set can have its members listed inside braces; one member gives a unit set, two a pair set. Infinite sets are generally defined by statement frames, so the reals whose square is under nine form the open interval from minus three to three. We need the empty set much as arithmetic needs zero; in passing, the authors note that the number four is usually defined as the set of zero, one, two and three.

Next, restricted variables. A variable is not allowed to take all objects as values; it can only take members of a certain set, called its domain. The domain is sometimes stated and more often implied, as the letter n customarily means an integer. Restricted variables are only abbreviations of unrestricted ones, and the two unfoldings differ: the universal case uses implication, the existential case uses and, and they must not be mixed up.

Finally ordered pairs and relations. The crucial property of a pair is that two are equal exactly when their first elements agree and their second elements agree, so one three is not three one. Since the graph of a relation is a set of ordered pairs, and every object is regarded as a set, it is efficient to take the graph to be the relation: a relation is simply a set of ordered pairs. From this come the domain, the range and the inverse, and all pairs with first element in A and second in B form the Cartesian product.

Part of a bilingual animated teaching series (English edition).
